analysis_name: Stage C Heat Priority Index (HPI) Sensitivity Analysis

scenarios.name: Thermal-Dominant (Heatwave Emergency)
scenarios.policy_rationale: Simulates acute emergency response mobilization during extreme heatwave alerts. Municipal disaster management prioritizes immediate, severe thermal exposure (60% weight) over chronic multi-year history or static neighborhood surface density.

scenarios.name: Persistence-Dominant (Infrastructure)
scenarios.policy_rationale: Simulates long-term municipal capital investment planning (e.g. permanent shade corridors, cool roofing subsidies). Prioritizes locations with chronic, repeated multi-year heat trapping (50% weight) over single-year temperature spikes or transient meteorological fluctuations.

scenarios.name: Nature-Deficit (Urban Greening)
scenarios.policy_rationale: Simulates urban forestry and ecological restoration planning. Focuses municipal resources on areas exhibiting severe canopy deficits (30% weight) and high impervious built surface density (20% weight) where nature-based interventions have the greatest biophysical cooling potential.

scenarios.name: Equal Component Weighting
scenarios.policy_rationale: Serves as an unweighted neutral baseline to evaluate whether the subjective 40/30/15/15 weighting scheme introduces disproportionate spatial distortion compared to an agnostic multi-criteria composite index.

scientific_caveats.sensitivity_vs_validation: Sensitivity analysis demonstrates the mathematical stability of spatial rankings under varied multi-criteria weighting assumptions. A high Spearman rank correlation (rho >= 0.88 across all scenarios) indicates algorithmic robustness, but DOES NOT PROVE that the baseline weights (40/30/15/15) are empirically optimal, physical ground truth, or causally linked to actual urban cooling outcomes.
scientific_caveats.no_retraining_or_mutation: Underlying thermal observations, Landsat surface reflectances, Sentinel spectral indices, and frozen ML estimators were kept strictly fixed. No model weights were retrained, no datasets were regenerated, and no database records were modified.
scientific_caveats.policy_guidance: Local municipal decision-makers should consider sensitivity bounds when allocating capital investments. Grid cells that remain in the Top 10% across all 4 scenarios represent consensus high-priority targets regardless of whether acute emergency, multi-year persistence, or ecological deficit priorities are adopted.
